mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the current month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS), or FEDFUNDS increases fail to precede declines in SPX 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In a robust labor market regime, the 20-day SPX returns show no correlation with the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction (Pearson's IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy via GDPC1 ) exceeding 3% suggests accelerating demand for goods and services, which elevates future earnings expectations and supports positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, GDPC1 growth does not predict SPX 5-day returns (p > 0.10 in Granger causality test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 200) indicates supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty and pushing 20-day S&P 500 returns into the negative.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% month-over-month and CPIAUCSL < 200 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During supply-side shocks, the interaction of INDPRO decline and low CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns (IC > -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, it signals a pause in rate hikes, lowering real discount rates and supporting positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 20-day average during previous hike periods (t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (proxy via HOUST) without a corresponding increase in job vacancies (not in catalog) suggests labor market imbalances that raise uncertainty and drive negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 15% in a single month
failure_condition: In periods of high HOUST volatility, the 20-day SPX returns show no significant negative relationship with the HOUST spike (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price indexes (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2% indicate accelerating inflation, which erodes real equity valuations and predicts negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 2% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 months, CPIAUCSL inflation does not precede negative 5-day SPX returns (Granger causality p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand indicators (e.g., GDPC1 < 1100B) suggests a dual supply-demand squeeze, raising risk premia and pushing 20-day S&P 500 returns into negative territory.
failure_condition: During such imbalances, the interaction of INDPRO decline and low GDPC1 does not predict negative 20-day SPX returns (IC > -0.1).
